name: Daichi Musō
equipment: Prayer beads (juzu) of the mountain temple
A scroll case of meditation sutras
A winter blanket and traveling robes
A set of common temple garb
features: Unarmored Defense (AC = 10 + Dexterity modifier + Wisdom modifier when wearing no armor or shield)
Martial Arts (use Dexterity for unarmed strikes and monk weapons; martial arts die is 1d4; bonus-action unarmed strike after Attack action)
Bushidō Discipline (a sōhei's vows of restraint, service, and martial readiness)
Discovery (Hermit feature: a unique and powerful insight gained in seclusion)

personality.traits: I am calm as a still pond, even when the world rages around me. ⛩️ I rise before dawn to sweep the path and breathe, and I find a lesson in every small thing. I would rather end a fight in one strike than draw it out.
personality.ideals: Harmony. The body and the spirit are one mountain; to perfect the fist is to perfect the heart. I defend the helpless and restrain the cruel, for that is the true sweep of the temple broom.
personality.bonds: The fire-mountain temple of Mount Hiei that raised me was put to the torch by a warlord's army, and my master died shielding the novices. I carry his prayer beads and his teachings, and I will not let his way be forgotten.
personality.flaws: My calm can curdle into detachment, and I sometimes meet others' pain with a serenity that looks like coldness. I am slow to anger — but when the line is crossed, my discipline can give way to a frightening, total focus.

appearance: A spare, deceptively gentle man of Hinomoto, his head shaved smooth in the manner of the warrior-monks, his frame all quiet sinew beneath simple robes. 🦊 He wears the layered gray-and-saffron garb of a sōhei, sleeves bound back for movement, a long bō staff worn smooth in his grip and a string of dark prayer beads looped about one wrist. His bare feet are calloused from a lifetime of mountain paths and temple floors. His expression is usually one of mild, attentive peace — but in a fight he moves with sudden, flowing economy, every strike landing exactly where it must and nowhere it need not.
backstory: Daichi Musō was left as an infant at the gate of a remote sōhei temple on the slopes of a holy fire-mountain, and the warrior-monks raised him as their own. He grew up sweeping the long stone stairs, drawing water before dawn, copying sutras by lamplight — and training, always training, in the empty-hand arts and the way of the staff that the sōhei wielded to defend their mountain from bandits and grasping lords. His master taught him that the perfected body was a vessel for a perfected spirit, and that a monk's violence must be the surgeon's stroke: precise, restrained, and only ever in defense of the defenseless. That peace shattered when a warlord, coveting the temple's land and resentful of its independence, sent an army up the mountain in the night. The halls burned; Daichi's master died with his arms spread before a huddle of young novices, buying them the moments they needed to flee. Daichi carried two of those children to safety and then walked down off the mountain for the first time in his life, his master's prayer beads in his hand. Now he wanders the floating world as a pilgrim and a guardian, seeking to honor his teacher's way — protecting the weak, calming the troubled, and meeting cruelty with a discipline as immovable as the mountain that made him.
